questiontext.text:
Data detective: what kind of column is this?

A survey of cassava farmers has been imported into R-Instat. Before producing summaries, you need to understand what the columns represent.

The extract below is illustrative. Each question version uses a different starting farmer ID and different ages.

Farmer IDAge (years)CountryInterview noteConsumption frequency
{@id1@}{@age1@}{@country1@}Prefers boiled cassavaSometimes
{@id2@}{@age2@}{@country2@}Prefers fried cassavaOften
{@id3@}{@age3@}{@country1@}Prefers boiled cassavaRarely
{@id4@}{@age4@}{@country2@}Prefers roasted cassavaSometimes

For this exercise, numeric means a measured quantity that is sensible to summarise numerically; character means text not yet organised into factor levels; and factor means a column with a defined set of categories. An ordered factor has categories with a meaningful order.

A. Predict: the identifier trap

The Farmer ID values contain only digits. Does that make their mean a meaningful summary of the farmers? [[input:predict]] [[validation:predict]] [[feedback:prtpredict]]

B. Classify the columns

Which kind of column is appropriate for Age (years)? [[input:agekind]] [[validation:agekind]] [[feedback:prtage]]

Which kind of column is appropriate for Country? [[input:countrykind]] [[validation:countrykind]] [[feedback:prtcountry]]

Which kind of column is appropriate for Interview note, as currently recorded in free text? [[input:notekind]] [[validation:notekind]] [[feedback:prtnote]]

Which kind of column is appropriate for Consumption frequency if its possible values are Rarely, Sometimes and Often? [[input:freqkind]] [[validation:freqkind]] [[feedback:prtfreq]]

C. Investigate the numbers

Calculate the mean of the four ages. Give your answer to two decimal places if necessary. [[input:meanage]] [[validation:meanage]] [[feedback:prtmean]]

[[hint title="Hint: mean age"]]

Add the four ages and divide by the number of farmers.

[[/hint]]

Why would calculating the mean of the Farmer ID column be misleading? [[input:idreason]] [[validation:idreason]] [[feedback:prtidreason]]

D. Interpret

Suppose R-Instat imported Farmer ID as a numeric column because every value contains digits. Which action best reflects its purpose in this dataset? [[input:idaction]] [[validation:idaction]] [[feedback:prtidaction]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Farmer ID identifies records. Although its values are written using digits and may be imported as numeric, it is not a measured quantity. Averaging {@id1@}, {@id2@}, {@id3@} and {@id4@} would not describe a typical farmer.

Age is numeric. Its mean in this extract is:

\[ \frac{{@age1@}+{@age2@}+{@age3@}+{@age4@}}{4}={@q_meanage@}. \]

Country is a factor: its values belong to a defined set of categories. Interview note is character data because it is recorded as free text. Consumption frequency is an ordered factor: Rarely, Sometimes and Often have a meaningful order.

The key distinction is between how a column happens to be stored and what its values mean. Farmer ID can be kept as an identifier (for example, as character data or as a numeric ID excluded from numerical summaries); it should not be treated as a measured quantity. Factor levels help organise repeated categories for summaries and graphs.

truefeedback.text: Correct: age is a numeric measurement.

falsefeedback.text: Age is measured in years, and its numerical summaries can be meaningful.

truefeedback.text: Correct: country is a factor with defined categories.

falsefeedback.text: Country labels identify groups; there is no natural numerical or ranked order.

truefeedback.text: Correct: Rarely, Sometimes and Often have a meaningful order.

falsefeedback.text: The categories have a natural order, although their spacing is not numerical.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Keep the identifier for linking and locating records, not numerical summaries.

falsefeedback.text: An identifier can be useful even though its numerical average is not.

truefeedback.text: Correct: a numerical-looking identifier is still a label.

falsefeedback.text: Ask whether the size or difference between two IDs measures anything about the farmers.

truefeedback.text: Correct. You have added the ages and divided by four.

falsefeedback.text: Add all four ages, then divide by four. Check that you did not average the IDs.

truefeedback.text: Correct: the notes are currently free text (character data).

falsefeedback.text: A free-text note is not yet a factor with a fixed set of levels.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Digits alone do not make an identifier a measurement.

falsefeedback.text: Think about what an ID represents, rather than how it is written.
